look_here_first: Look at the mature pod cluster first: strongly sickle-curved, comparatively BROAD pods about 15–32 mm long × 4.5–7 mm wide. Heads commonly have 20–70 flowers. Upright to spreading robust stems can reach 20–150 cm.

key_traits.label: Growth flower fruit
key_traits.text: Much more robust and taller on average than prairie bundleflower, but size alone varies. Leaves typically with 5–18 pairs of pinnae; 5 stamens, flowers in dense heads. Several short broad crescent/sickle-like seedpods crowd together in a characteristic tight bundle. Often moistish clay/ditches/stream bottoms.

key_traits.label: Distinguishing characters
key_traits.text: D. leptolobus has fewer flowers per head (4–12) and long straight NARROW pods 35–70 × 2–3 mm; D. velutinus has 10 rather than 5 stamens and straighter longer pods.

key_traits.label: Shared genus
key_traits.text: Unarmed perennial Fabaceae with compound bipinnate leaves and small brushlike heads, often a petiolar/rachis gland, flat legume pods. Pod structure diagnostic.
